title: Life and property of the individual
statement: I believe that the life and property of the individual.

title: Reality is the final test
statement: A belief should not change because of pressure, popularity, or emotion alone. It should change when reality shows it is false.
evidence: Truth claims need standards outside personal preference.
Stable reasoning becomes possible when evidence can overrule ego.
disproof: Show a class of important beliefs where objective evidence and observed outcomes should not carry decisive weight.

title: Context matters as much as facts
statement: Raw facts can mislead when stripped from timing, incentives, or surrounding conditions. Honest interpretation requires context.
evidence: The same statistic can support opposite conclusions when context is hidden.
Most bad-faith arguments rely on selective framing instead of full reality.
disproof: Show that context regularly makes reasoning less accurate instead of more accurate in high-stakes decisions.

title: Changing your mind is strength
statement: When better evidence appears, revising a belief is a sign of intellectual integrity, not weakness.
evidence: Stubborn consistency often protects identity rather than truth.
Public reasoning improves when updates are rewarded instead of mocked.
disproof: Show that belief revision predictably harms trust even when the new position is better supported.
rulingNote: Refined to emphasize public trust grows when reasoning is visible, not when you never update.
